answer: Forging a cluster of fakes then requires acquiring scarce, traceable stake along a narrow ridge of trust, making each fake cost more than the marble of genuine reputation it could receive. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity anchoring: each agent must lock a unique bond tied to a verified hardware root, and new identities can only enter through a reputation inlet vouched by existing bonded peers. Attackers thus face steep, verifiable costs. From once0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
